## Execution tips

- Prefer straight upper-body sections below the bottle shoulders for continuous pad contact. Avoid caps, sloped shoulders and bottom ridges to reduce slipping and leave room for the bottle bottom to enter the bin.
- The yellow bottle on the right is beside the blue-decorated bottle. Approach from the side with more clearance, opening slightly wider than the grasp region. Confirm in side views that the fingers straddle the body before closing to avoid toppling it or hitting its neighbor.
- During horizontal transport, keep the bottle base above clutter and the bin rim along the route. Avoid sweeping into the hammer and white block near the front of the table or catching the bottle base on the rim.
- Only part of the bin opening is visible initially. Use the left-side view to confirm its inner boundary and bring the horizontal footprint of the bottom and body inside before lowering, avoiding resting on the table edge or bin wall.
- Lower the release height and leave clearance from the bin walls and bottles already inside to reduce rebound from collisions. After release, check that the bottle falls farther inside without catching on the rim or bouncing out.
